tax.text: He supported extending the 2001 and 2003 tax cuts, which lowered tax rates.
tax.quote: Tax relief is vital to encouraging economic growth. Congressman Bishop believes that tax relief is a bi-partisan issue and has routinely crossed the aisle to do what is best for American families. For example, he strongly supported the extension of the 2001 and 2003 tax cuts, which lowered tax rates across the board for all Americans and propelled economic growth in Georgia.

wages.text: He cosponsored the Raise the Wage Act, which proposed increasing the federal minimum wage.
wages.quote: To provide for increases in the Federal minimum wage, and for other purposes.

debt.text: He said Social Security and Medicare solvency should use both new revenue and long-term structural reforms.
debt.quote: Such options should include a balanced approach such as a mix of revenue raisers but also long-term structural reforms.

housing.text: He supports increasing the supply of affordable housing and expanding rural and veteran housing opportunities.
housing.quote: I support legislation to help homeowners avoid foreclosure, stop predatory and irresponsible mortgage loan practices, increase the supply of affordable housing, expand veteran and rural housing opportunities, promote fair housing education and enforcement activities, and finance community development initiatives.

schools.text: He reports securing federal funding for schools, libraries, and related public education programs.
schools.quote: Congressman Bishop has secured millions of dollars for education programs, including funding for new schools and libraries, after-school programs, STEM education initiatives, school nutrition and physical education programs, as well as family counseling and youth mentoring.

safety.text: He supports resources for law enforcement and also supports prevention programs for at-risk youth.
safety.quote: Research has consistently shown that investment in prevention-based strategies that reach at-risk youth before they ever become involved in criminal activity are the most effective way to reduce crime in the long-term.

guns.text: He voted for the Bipartisan Background Checks Act on passage in 2019.
guns.quote: Vote Question: On Passage Bipartisan Background Checks Act Vote Type: Yea-And-Nay Status: Passed

abortion.text: He cosponsored the Women’s Health Protection Act, which protects access to abortion services.
abortion.quote: To protect a person’s ability to determine whether to continue or end a pregnancy, and to protect a health care provider’s ability to provide abortion services.

gender.text: He voted against the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act, which would set participation rules based on sex at birth.
gender.quote: Vote Question: On Passage Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act Vote Type: Yea-And-Nay Status: Passed

cannabis.text: He voted for passage of the MORE Act in 2020.
cannabis.quote: Vote Question: On Passage MORE Act Vote Type: Yea-And-Nay

health.text: He supports the Affordable Care Act, expanded community health centers, and extending coverage to unemployed people.
health.quote: He strongly supports the Affordable Care Act because it makes significant strides toward improving the health and well-being of the citizens of Georgia’s 2nd District.

energy.text: He supports expanding domestic oil and natural gas supplies and protecting consumers from energy costs.
energy.quote: That’s why Congressman Bishop supports initiatives that promote conservation and energy efficiency, utilize alternative energy sources, expand our domestic supplies of oil and natural gas, and above all, protect consumers.

voting.text: He voted against the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act, which would impose additional eligibility requirements for voter registration.
voting.quote: Vote Question: On Passage Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act Vote Type: Recorded Vote Status: Passed

tax.text: He pledged not to raise marginal income tax rates for individuals or businesses and not to eliminate tax deductions.
tax.quote: Matt has pledged not to Increase Tax Marginal Income Tax Rates for Individuals or Businesses. He also pledges to not reduce or eliminate Tax Deductions.

debt.text: He pledged to sponsor a bill to protect, stabilize and fund Social Security and Medicare.
debt.quote: Matt pledges to Not Seek Re-Election unless he Sponsors a Bill for Seniors that will protect, stabilize and fund America's Social Security and Medicare his 1st Term.

safety.text: He pledges to sponsor legislation to protect, empower, and aid law enforcement.
safety.quote: Matt pledges to Not Seek Re-Election unless he Sponsors a Bill that will protect, empower and give aide to America's Law Enforcement of Americans his 1st Term.

immigration.text: He said his proposed bill would let undocumented workers earn citizenship by paying taxes.
immigration.quote: It offers a path for undocumented workers to pay their taxes and earn their citizenship.

guns.text: He pledged to sponsor legislation protecting gun owners’ rights.
guns.quote: Matt pledges to Not Seek Re-Election unless he Sponsors a Bill that will protect the Rights of Gun Owners in American his 1st Term in Office.

abortion.text: He said he would fight for unborn children and pledged to sponsor a bill to better protect them.
abortion.quote: More abortion deaths than both the World War Casualties combined. Matt will fight for the unborn.

health.text: His proposed legislation would expand Medicare coverage to dental, vision, and hearing care.
health.quote: Routine dental services; Vision care including annual exams and corrective lenses; Hearing assessments and hearing aid devices.
